subject: Birds on telegraph wires drawn in front elevation: two poles carry one wire per scale degree, every perched bird sounds its wire, and birds in the air are hopping between wires.
controls: cohere: how closely the birds bunch along the span and onto neighbouring wires (position: spacing from ~56 px to ~10 px between birds).
speed: how many birds are off their wires mid-hop at once, each with its dashed hop path (count: none at 0.25 to five of eight at 4.00).
scatter: birds that perch far out on the span and on distant wires, away from the bunch (position, up to the full span).
scale: the number of wires strung between the poles (count: 11 to 25), octave wires labelled at the left pole.
reference: library/theseus-tower/README.md (known object from clean primitives, line drawing, only the struck part moves)
risks: Stretch: P11 is for drum kits, an instrument people know by sight. A player has no instrument. The exception argument is that birds on a wire is already a picture everyone reads as notes on a staff, so the wires work as the 'instrument' and each wire has its own place; that's an analogy, not the pattern's reason, and it may simply not fit.
Bird silhouettes are the icon trap craft.md warns about; the line has to stay a drafted elevation (one outline, hairline wires, no cartoon eyes) or it becomes clip-art.
chrom strings 25 wires 5 px apart: under the 6 px stack spacing in accessibility.md. Chrom would need a two-octave fold or a smaller range.
The poles and insulators are static scenery that does nothing for the sound.
